title: FLASH: Faint Lenses from Associated Selection with Herschel
question: Can high-resolution ALMA Band 7 continuum observations confirm the lensing nature of 86 faint Herschel submillimetre sources (S500 = 15-85 mJy) identified through statistical association with foreground VIKING near-infrared galaxies, and what does this imply for the total number of lenses across Herschel surveys?

data.sensitivity: 72 uJy/beam (untapered continuum); 137 uJy/beam (0.5 arcsec tapered continuum)

what.value: H-ATLAS GAMA-12 sub-mm positions and 250, 350, 500 um photometry

evidence.quote: This survey is based on the H-ATLAS 12-hour equatorial field (Eales et al. 2010; Valiante et al. 2016), which has good coverage with the VIKING NIR and the optical KIDS survey.

recipe.goal: Select the FLASH sample of 86 faint Herschel lens candidates
recipe.method: Start from 35,512 H-ATLAS GAMA-12 sources; remove sources within 10 arcsec of NVSS radio sources; fit modified blackbody SEDs to 250, 350, 500 um fluxes and require z_phot > 2.0; apply VIKING Ks-band likelihood ratio and reliability estimator; require <0.1% (~3.1 sigma) probability that VIKING and Herschel redshifts overlap; select highest reliability sources in 10 mJy S500 bins within 10 degrees of a single phase centre.
assumptions: Submillimetre photometric redshift uncertainty Delta z = 0.13(1 + z)

recipe.goal: Extract 1.1 mm continuum positions and flux densities
recipe.method: Run CASA IMFIT iteratively on the 0.5 arcsec tapered continuum images until no obvious sources (> 3 sigma) remain in the residual image.
key_parameters: Residual threshold = 3 sigma on 0.5 arcsec tapered image

recipe.goal: Classify lensing grade (A, B, C) via visual morphology, angular separation, and annulus curve-of-growth analysis
recipe.method: Visually inspect ALMA maps overlaid on VIKING images to identify arcs/rings or offsets between 0.2 and 2 arcsec from the central VIKING galaxy (37 A-grade sources). Then perform an annulus curve-of-growth SNR analysis (Equation 6) with annulus widths of 0.15, 0.3, and 0.5 arcsec out to 5.5 arcsec around the VIKING position to detect faint (> 5 sigma) ring-like features (identifying 3 additional A-grade lenses: FLASH-30, -34, -75). Classify remaining sources into B-grade and C-grade.
key_parameters: A-grade angular offset range: 0.2 to 2 arcsec from VIKING galaxy (without bright VIKING counterpart at ALMA position)
Annulus widths: 0.15, 0.3, and 0.5 arcsec; detection threshold > 5 sigma
assumptions: Astrometric accuracy of ALMA and VIKING is < 0.1 arcsec

recipe.goal: Search for spectral line features in tapered ALMA data cubes
recipe.method: Visually inspect spectra in the 0.5 arcsec tapered data cubes at source extraction positions, then perform per-source aperture photometry to extract emission or absorption lines and compare with sub-mm/VIKING photometric redshifts.

recipe.goal: Estimate foreground lensing halo masses and halo-to-stellar mass ratios
recipe.method: Use the observed weighted-average angular separation between VIKING and ALMA sources as an estimate of the Einstein radius theta_E in a Singular Isothermal Sphere (SIS) model (Equation 7) to compute total lensing mass M and compare with VIKING stellar masses M_*.
key_parameters: Halo virial radius definition r_200 = 3M / (4 * pi * 200 * rho_crit(z_l))
assumptions: Flat Lambda-CDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.315, Omega_Lambda = 0.685, h = 0.674
Single Isothermal Sphere (SIS) mass profile with observed angular separation taken as Einstein radius theta_E

recipe.goal: Derive cumulative 500 um lensed source counts and extrapolate to full H-ATLAS survey
recipe.method: Apply the ALMA-confirmed lensing success ratio of FLASH across the reliability-flux regime representative of the 53.56 sq. deg. GAMA-12 field to compute cumulative lensed number counts, correct the lowest two flux bins for 250 um catalogue redshift incompleteness, and extrapolate to the 660 sq. deg. H-ATLAS survey.
key_parameters: GAMA-12 field area = 53.56 sq. deg.; total H-ATLAS area = 660 sq. deg.
assumptions: Complete VIKING-level NIR coverage across the 660 sq. deg. H-ATLAS fields

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of confirmed A-grade gravitational lenses in FLASH sample

evidence.quote: Our high-resolution observations (0.15 arcsec) confirm 47 per cent of the initial candidates as gravitational lenses, while lensing cannot be excluded across the remaining sample.
The ALMA observations are able to confirm 40 (47 per cent) of these sources to be strong lenses (A-grade lens candidates).

answer_key.quantity: Number of confirmed A-grade gravitational lenses

evidence.quote: We robustly identify 40 lensed sources (A-grade), at 47 per cent of the total sample.
The ALMA observations are able to confirm 40 (47 per cent) of these sources to be strong lenses (A-grade lens candidates).
In 23 cases, there are some tentative indications of lensing, which cannot be confirmed with current observations (B-grade).
For an additional 23 (27 per cent) sources, there are tentative indications of lensing, however our ALMA observations are not able to conclusively indicate lensing (B-grade lens candidates).
For the remaining 23 cases, the ALMA observations provide no indications of gravitational lensing (C-grade).
For the final 23 (27 per cent), it remains unclear whether these sources are lensed (C-grade lens candidates).

answer_key.quantity: Average foreground lensing halo mass of A-grade candidates (log10 M/M_sun)

evidence.quote: We find average lensing masses (log 𝑀/𝑀⊙ = 12.9 ± 0.5) in line with previous experiments

evidence.loc: 4.3 The lensed galaxies of the FLASH sample
evidence.quote: The average mass for the A-grade lens candidates is log10 𝑀/𝑀⊙ = 12.9 ± 0.5, and lies approximately one order of magnitude below the C-grade sources.

answer_key.quantity: Halo-to-stellar mass ratio of A-grade lens candidates

Our method will be able to find ∼ 3000 lensed sources over the entire H-ATLAS field

score_reason: The ALMA data are public (2019.1.01784.S), full target and extracted photometry catalogues are provided in Tables 1 and 3, and the imaging (Briggs robust=2.0, 0.5 arcsec taper), flux extraction (CASA IMFIT to 3 sigma), classification criteria, and SIS mass equations are clearly described. Minor deductions for missing CASA/tclean parameters and exact window definitions for the spectral line extractions and number-count extrapolation.
rediscovery_reason: Public single-project ALMA dataset (2019.1.01784.S) with a straightforward pipeline+CASA imaging and IMFIT photometry workflow, explicit geometric/morphological lens grading rules, and well-defined numerical benchmarks (1.1 mm flux densities for 86 fields, 47% A-grade lens fraction, and mean log M/M_sun = 12.9 +/- 0.5).
